newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: S.Africa hopes for world effort on ex-Zaire.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa hopes for world effort on ex-Zaire.

text.p: South African Deputy Foreign Minister Aziz Pahad said on Monday he hoped an Organisation of African Unity (OAU) summit in Zimbabwe would decide on international help for the former Zaire.
Pahad, who made the remarks to South African state radio, is in Harare for the summit which starts on Monday.

"The task in the new Congo is so great that South Africa will not be able to help on its own," Pahad said, adding South Africa would prefer to help Laurent Kabila's Democratic Republic of Congo as part of a world initiative.

"We would think it should be an OAU-United Nations effort because world institutions like the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund, and the United Nations as a whole, would have to play a role.
"We hope that at the summit which starts today, some decisions will be taken in relation to how we can coordinate an international effort," Pahad said.
He said South Africa had identified areas in which it felt it could assist Kabila's new government get the country back on its feet.

"We've had discussions with several of our ministries, including the reserve bank, the department of trade and industry, the department of finance, constitutional affairs, to see whether we can put together a team that can go on an initial visit just to advise them on the way forward," Pahad said.
"We have put together a team but it will be dependent on discussions we have with the alliance in Harare today on the nature of when the delegation would go and what would be its overall purpose."
South Africa mediated between Kabila and former President Mobutu Sese Seko, who abandonned power to Kabila's rebels last month in a relatively bloodless exit from 32 years in office.
